description:
Variation of condition 1 (Approved Drawings) attached to planning permission ref 2026/0290 dated 17/06/2026 for the erection of a new hipped & pitched roof to provide additional
accommodation to the dwelling within the existing single-storey building. The variation would alter the window and door arrangement at the southern and northern elevations.
decision_conditions: <p>The Development hereby permitted shall only be carried out and completed strictly in accordance with the submitted plans hereby approved and any subsequent approval of details.</p><p>REASON: To ensure that the development hereby permitted is carried out in full accordance with the plans hereby approved.</p>

<p>The development hereby permitted must be begun not later than the expiration of three years from 17/06/2026, being the date that application ref: 2026/0290 was granted.&nbsp;</p><p>REASON: In order to comply with the provisions of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (as amended).</p>

<p>The roof light within the new altered roof form, hereby approved, shall be obscurely glazed to the satisfaction of the local planning authority and permanently fixed shut.&nbsp;</p><p>REASON: In the interests of the amenities of adjoining residents.&nbsp;</p>

<div style="">Prior to the first occupation of the extension, hereby permitted, a permanent, robust scheme for the prevention of gutter blockage from leaf litter, derived from the adjacent retained tree, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority (LPA).</div><div style=""><br>The scheme shall specify the type and design of gutter guards, leaf traps, or filtration systems to be permanently installed on all guttering of the new building. These measures shall be designed to effectively prevent the accumulation of tree litter in the gutters and downpipes, thereby reducing the need for future requests to prune or fell the retained trees due to amenity issues.<br></div><div style=""><br>The approved gutter guards/filtration systems shall be installed and fully operational prior to the first occupation of the new extension.</div><div style=""><br>REASON: To ensure that the design of the new building is compatible with the presence of mature retained trees, thereby safeguarding their long-term health and contribution to the local environment and preventing the unnecessary future loss or adverse pruning of trees due to foreseeable amenity issues.</div>

<p>All new works, and works of making good to the retained fabric, whether internal or external, shall be finished to match the original work with regard to the methods used and to material, dimensions, composition, form, colour, finish and profile, and in the case of brickwork, facebond and pointing.</p><p>REASON: To preserve or enhance the character and appearance of the conservation area.&nbsp;</p>
